problem: "The matching current is I(z) = ..." uses the word 'matching', which in RF already means impedance matching; a student may think the equation applies only to a matched line.

P⁺ = |V⁺|²/(2Z0) is correct only if |V⁺| is the peak amplitude of the phasor; with an RMS phasor the answer is twice too small. The chapter never says which convention it uses. The efficiency η = e^(−2αl) also assumes a matched load, which is not stated.
fix: Write: P⁺ = |V⁺|²/(2Z0) W for real Z0, where |V⁺| is the peak amplitude (use |V⁺|²/Z0 if |V⁺| is RMS). Then: for a load matched to Z0 there is no reflection, and a line of length l delivers a fraction e^(−2αl) of the input power, so η = e^(−2αl).

where: Exam traps, last trap but one
problem: The clause "which then makes the two waves add instead of travelling opposite ways" is garbled: a sign error makes the forward and backward current terms add, it does not stop the waves travelling in opposite directions.
fix: "Dropping the minus sign in dV/dz = −(R + jωL)I, or in the backward current term of I(z), which then makes the two current terms add instead of subtract."

problem: Saying "When R/L > G/C the attenuation rises with frequency" implies that attenuation does not rise with frequency otherwise. For a passive line α increases with frequency for every practical ratio of R/L to G/C; the comparison R/L against G/C decides whether conductor loss or dielectric loss dominates, not whether α rises.
fix: "Attenuation rises with frequency on this cable, so the high-frequency components are attenuated more than the low ones and the pulse edges round off. The condition R/L > G/C means conductor loss, which grows with frequency, is larger than dielectric loss. Loading coils add series inductance, which raises L and lowers R/L towards G/C, flattening α against frequency."
